notes: Partition re-checked: all 35 source and 38 target IDs covered exactly once.

The waw of וְיַעֲשֵׂם takes *which* under rule 17's settled ruling for a waw plus a finite verb with no explicit subject pronoun standing in the recast clause, and the object suffix, resumed once by that same word, is the unrendered occurrence under rule 22. Giving *which* to the suffix under rule 18 was the competing reading and is worth recording, since rule 17's carve-out names an explicit subject pronoun rather than an object suffix.

The italic *his* is the assimilated article's under rule 41: it stands where the phrase's *the* would stand and no suffix or other possessive morpheme stands on חַיִּים to license it; the italic corroborates without deciding (rule 7).

מִסְפַּר takes a bare *all* with no *of* written, and the phrase's single *the* stands before *days*, so it is the supplied determiner on the construct יְמֵי (rule 29); הֶבְלוֹ is rendered attributively as *vain* under rule 28.

אֲשֶׁר takes the connective *for* opening the second question rather than being left unrepresented beside an `added` word, which is what counting the clause's connectives against its conjunction morphemes supports. The Hebrew gloss note was read and set aside (rule 38).
